n: Yolk sac tumor of the testis
dx: Yolk sac tumor of the testis

ww.Embryonal carcinoma: Embryonal carcinoma shows crowded, overlapping, markedly pleomorphic cells with necrosis and hemorrhage. It lacks the glomerulus-like body with a central vessel; here a more uniform lining of cells surrounds open spaces and vascular cores.
ww.Seminoma: Seminoma is a sheet of uniform fried-egg cells with clear cytoplasm and lymphocytes in the septa. This tumor instead forms papillae and spaces lined by cuboidal to columnar cells around vascular cores.
ww.Choriocarcinoma: Choriocarcinoma combines large multinucleated syncytiotrophoblasts with smaller cytotrophoblasts and extensive hemorrhage. Here a single type of epithelial cell lines papillary and glandular spaces around small vessels.
ww.Mature teratoma: Mature teratoma contains well-differentiated tissues from all three germ layers, such as glands, cartilage and skin. This field is one population of primitive epithelium arranged in papillae, with no mature tissues.

look: Scan for papillae with a blood vessel running through their core. Tumor cells line open spaces and wrap these cores, and the best examples look like a glomerulus: a central capillary, a cuff of tumor cells and a space around them. That is a Schiller-Duval body, the signature of yolk sac tumor, which secretes AFP and is the most common testicular tumor in boys younger than 3.
findings: Schiller-Duval body: a papilla with a central capillary full of red blood cells, wrapped by tumor cells and projecting into an open space, gives a glomerulus-like structure near the lower left of the field.

Papillary architecture: branching papillae with fibrovascular cores are lined by cuboidal to columnar tumor cells with dark nuclei, and open spaces between them give the lacy pattern typical of yolk sac tumor.

Lining epithelium: the cells that cover the papillae are crowded, with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and prominent nuclei, a primitive epithelium that secretes alpha-fetoprotein, so the serum AFP is raised.
